symptoms: Global-route overflow >2% concentrated in macro-to-macro channels and around macro pins, with near-zero overflow in standard-cell-only regions - shape indicates pin-access/channel-width problem not overall utilization
Detailed route aborts with 1000s of opens/shorts after post-CTS looked clean (overflow 0.5-1% but with high local density >90%) - shape indicates layer promotion / track blockage vs true routability
Early congestion map shows horizontal overflow > vertical overflow by 3-5x in one metal layer, often M3/M4 - shape points to power-strap or PG mesh blocking preferred routing direction

candidate_causes.cause: Macro channel width too narrow and macro pins not aligned on tracks
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Plot macro halo + channel width vs min required for pin escape; if all overflow edges touch macro boundaries and pin density heatmap spikes at same location, it's channel/pin access
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Increase channel width 1-2x row height, spread or rotate macros, add placement blockage to keep cells out of channel

candidate_causes.cause: High placement utilization >75-80% in congestion hotspot
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Overlay utilization heatmap with overflow map; if overflow cells correlate with >85% density and cell count >1.2x average, it's utilization-driven; check if 28nm allows 75% vs 7nm needs 65-70%
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add partial placement blockage 10-15%, reduce target density, or expand floorplan 2-3%

candidate_causes.cause: Power-ground mesh over-blocking routing tracks
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Toggle PG visibility in congestion viewer; if overflow disappears when M4-M7 PG straps set non-visible and layer-wise overflow drops >50% on those layers, it's PG blocking
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Thin PG straps from 2um to 1um in hotspot, add slots, switch some straps to higher layers, or increase PG pitch

candidate_causes.cause: Pin access blocked by cell orientation or insufficient via access layers
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Run pin-access checker / DRC in pin region; if violations are M1-M2 spacing or via1 enclosure at standard-cell pins and not global nets, and reports list same 2-3 library cells, it's library pin access
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Swap cell orientation, use alternative VT or double-height cells, allow extra access layer, add pin-access-aware placement spacing

candidate_causes.cause: Signal layer assignment / non-default rule too aggressive
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check overflow by layer; if one layer shows >80% of overflows and that layer has non-default width/spacing rule or wrong preferred direction, compare to route-rule report
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Relax NDR, change layer range for high-fanout nets, reserve high layers for long nets

ordering_rationale: Veteran checks cheapest visual overlays first (channel, utilization, PG) before expensive pin-access or rule analysis because 80% of congestion is placement-channel-PG interaction.
classic_trap: Immediately dropping utilization globally or adding routing halo everywhere, which hurts timing and area, when real cause is 2-3 macro pins aligned badly blocking one channel.

symptoms: Few paths failing with large negative slack -400ps to -800ps, all share same startpoint cluster or same long combinational depth >20 stages - shape indicates logic-depth or mis-placed macro

Many paths (1000s) failing with small negative slack -20ps to -80ps across unrelated hierarchies, TNS large but WNS small - shape indicates global constraint / clock skew / OCV derate / utilization drag
Failing paths show sudden jump in slack at block boundary or at clock-domain crossing, with 0.5-1ns delta on one net - shape indicates budget/SDC or clock insertion mismatch, not cell speed

candidate_causes.cause: Logic depth too high for target frequency / poor mapping
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Report path depth and cell delay vs net delay split; if cell delay >70% and stage count >18-22 at 1GHz-equivalent and path is in same module, check if same function has faster architectural option
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Restructure logic, add pipeline stage, use faster VT, replace with low-VT or HVT mix, enable useful-skew

candidate_causes.cause: Bad placement / long net detour around macros or congestion
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Plot failing path physical flyline vs Manhattan; if net length >3x straight distance or path goes around macro channel and net delay >50% of path, it's placement
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Create placement bound near driver, add placement guide, unplace and re-place with timing-driven weighting

candidate_causes.cause: Clock skew / insertion delay mismatch between launch and capture
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check clock arrival times in timing report: if skew >15% of cycle and failing paths all have common clock gating cell or different CTS insertion, and skew-adjusted slack recovers when ideal clocks used
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Re-balance CTS, adjust clock latency target, add useful skew, fix gating-cell placement

candidate_causes.cause: Incorrect SDC / missing multicycle / false path / input delay
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If paths are cross-clock or have large input delay and fail only at boundary, check if constraint has missing set_multicycle_path or set_false_path; run constraint checker and compare to architect spec - at 28nm many false paths were real, at 7nm more MB timing budgets
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Fix SDC, derive realistic block-to-block budget from top-level STA, add clock uncertainty margin

candidate_causes.cause: OCV / derate / voltage-drop pessimism
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Compare PBA vs GBA slack and compare nominal vs derated; if PBA recovers >30% of violation and derate >10% at 28nm or >15% at 7nm, and IR map shows overlap, it's pessimism/IR-induced
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Reduce OCV margin with AOCV/POCV, improve IR, add margin recovery in ECO

ordering_rationale: Veteran checks constraints and clock shape first because a single wrong SDC explains 1000s of paths cheaply, then distinguishes depth vs placement by cell-vs-net delay split before touching logic.
classic_trap: Treating a wall of -30ps failures as needing logic restructuring when it's actually a clock skew or derate issue; sizing up cells makes congestion and power worse with no WNS gain.

symptoms: Hold violations appear immediately after CTS with ideal clocks off, count 100s-1000s but WNS small -20ps to -100ps, paths are short 2-5 stages
Hold fails only at block-to-block interfaces or on scan-shift paths, not inside random logic - shape points to interface clock skew or scan hold
Hold slack improves when setup is improved or when cell delay increases - inverse correlation indicates over-aggressive low-VT / high-leakage bias for setup closure

candidate_causes.cause: Short data path vs long clock path after CTS - clock insertion larger than data
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Report data vs clock insertion for failing endpoints; if clock arrival > data arrival + hold margin and path is same clock domain, and failure disappears with ideal zero-skew clocks
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Insert delay cells or buffer in short data path, add hold-aware useful skew, reduce clock insertion to short-path flops

candidate_causes.cause: Over-aggressive setup fixing with low-VT / HVT swap and sizing down creating fast paths
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check library mix: if failing cells are all LVT or SVT and setup-fixed region overlaps hold region, and delay distribution shows bimodal fast tail
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Swap to higher VT on short path, add delay buffers with hold-fixed flag, constrain ECO to not touch hold-critical

candidate_causes.cause: Interface clock skew between blocks / between functional and test clocks
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If hold fails only at block boundary and launch/capture clocks are different generated clocks or scan clocks, compare inter-clock skew vs intra-clock; check clock definitions in SDC for missing inter-clock hold uncertainty
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add inter-clock hold uncertainty 10-15% of cycle, balance interface clocks, add lockup latch or delay at boundary

candidate_causes.cause: Missing hold in SDC or unrealistic hold uncertainty = 0
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check SDC for set_min_delay or hold uncertainty; if uncertainty is 0 and design has >500MHz at 28nm or >1GHz at 7nm, constraints are optimistic; compare to foundry recommended hold margin
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add realistic hold uncertainty 50-100ps at 28nm, 30-60ps at 7nm, apply set_fix_hold on interface

candidate_causes.cause: High OCV derate for hold creates pessimistic fast corner
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check if hold fails only with OCV on and passes at 0 derate; if fast corner derate >10% and common-clock pessimism removal not applied, it's derate-induced
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Enable CCP removal, adjust min derate to 0.95-0.98, fix true short paths only

ordering_rationale: Hold is cheaper to diagnose than setup - check clock arrival and SDC uncertainty first (minutes) because most hold walls are clock-related, then examine fast-path cell mix before inserting buffers everywhere.
classic_trap: Fixing hold by blindly inserting thousands of buffers before CTS stability, which then breaks setup and congestion; correct order is fix clock skew first, then only truly short data paths.

symptoms: Dynamic IR drop heatmap shows >80-100mV drop (>10% VDD at 28nm, >8% at 7nm) localized in 50um x 50um hotspots under high toggle activity, correlating with setup timing degradation
Static IR drop high in narrow channels between macros where PG straps are thin and no C4 bumps nearby - shape is stripe following PG mesh, not cell activity
Vectorless analysis clean but vector-based dynamic shows violations - shape indicates workload-dependent simultaneous switching, not static PG resistance

candidate_causes.cause: Insufficient PG strap width or pitch in hotspot
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Overlay PG map with IR map; if IR drop contours follow PG pitch and worst drop is mid-pitch away from straps, and resistance calculation shows >2x expected, it's strap density
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Widen straps, reduce pitch 20-30%, add top-layer mesh, add bump if possible

candidate_causes.cause: High toggle / high capacitance cells clustered
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If dynamic drop correlates with toggle rate >30% and cell power density map, and same cells appear in power report top 5%, and vector-based shows same hotspot as activity
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Spread high-drive cells, decluster clock gates, add placement spacing, lower frequency on hotspot block

candidate_causes.cause: Weak C4 bump / package ball assignment far from hotspot
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Plot distance to nearest power bump; if worst IR is >150-200um from nearest bump in flip-chip and bump map shows gap, it's bump limited - common at 28nm with sparse bumps vs 7nm with dense bump array
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add or move bumps, add ring, improve package RDL, add on-chip decap near hotspot

candidate_causes.cause: Insufficient decap / high di/dt
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If IR is dynamic-only, high-frequency component >50mV transient and decap density <10-15% in hotspot, and dI/dt report shows large current step
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add decap cells 5-10% in hotspot, add intrinsic decap, spread clock edges

candidate_causes.cause: Via stack resistance / thin lower-layer PG
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check via drop contribution: if drop on M1-M3 is >40% of total and lower-layer PG uses single vias, it's via stack - compare via count and via resistance table
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Double via, use via arrays, thicken lower PG, add more via transitions to upper mesh

ordering_rationale: Check PG geometry and bump distance first (visual, minutes) before activity-driven causes because fixing straps/decap is layout-only and avoids functional rework.
classic_trap: Assuming IR drop is always dynamic activity and spreading cells, when real cause is static resistance due to missing via arrays or PG straps cut by routing blockage, which spreading cells makes worse.

symptoms: Clock insertion delay >30-40% of cycle or skew >10-12% of cycle after CTS, with long flat skew histogram - indicates unbalanced or over-constrained tree
Clock has large number of buffers (>3x expected) and high power, yet skew still high - shape indicates conflicting skew targets or over-shielding / blockage
Post-CTS hold violations explode while setup improves - shape indicates clock delayed to fix setup but created short-path hold, common when useful skew not constrained

candidate_causes.cause: Clock gating cells placed far from fanout or clustered creating imbalance
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Report clock gate fanout and location; if one gate drives >50% of sinks and gate is at edge of block or behind macro, and insertion to that branch is 2x other branches, it's gating placement
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Place clock gates at centroid of fanout, clone gating cells, add soft guide to keep in CTS region

candidate_causes.cause: Macro or routing blockage blocks clock routing - clock detours
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Overlay clock routing with placement blockages and macro keepout; if clock routes go around macro channel and route length >1.5x Manhattan and layer is congested M3/M4, it's blockage
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Create clock routing channel, allow CTS to punch through soft blockage, move macro slightly

candidate_causes.cause: Over-constrained skew target / latency target too tight
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If skew target <50ps at 28nm or <20ps at 7nm and tool reports unable to meet with buffer limit, and relaxed target 100ps still meets setup, target is over-tight
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Relax skew target to 80-120ps at 28nm, 30-50ps at 7nm, relax max insertion, allow useful skew

candidate_causes.cause: Multiple clock domains mixed or generated clocks with wrong relationships
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If report shows clock domain crossing inside CTS tree or generated clocks not defined as -master, and latency differences >500ps between related clocks
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Fix SDC create_generated_clock relationships, separate CTS for each domain, set inter-clock balance false where needed

candidate_causes.cause: Insufficient routing resources for clock - non-default rule blocking
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If clock uses NDR double-spacing and overflow on clock layer >0 and clock DRCs increase post-CTS, check NDR impact on track availability
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Relax clock NDR in congested region, reserve two tracks for clock, use higher layers for trunk

ordering_rationale: Check SDC and skew targets first (minutes) because wrong generated-clock relationship or unrealistic skew target explains large delay skew cheaply, then check physical blockage and gating placement which require layout changes.
classic_trap: Tightening skew target even more when skew is high, causing tool to insert even more buffers and power, when real cause is a single gating cell far from its sinks or a blockage - looser target with better placement actually improves skew.

symptoms: DRC count >5000 after detailed route, dominated by short / spacing >80% on 1-2 layers, clustered near macro pins or in 2-3 small windows - shape indicates local pin access not global routing
DRCs are mostly via enclosure or cut spacing and appear only after adding via arrays / double vias - shape indicates via rule vs manufacturing grid
DRCs persist after 3-4 detail route iterations with same locations not moving - shape indicates unresolvable by router, needs placement or floorplan fix

candidate_causes.cause: Pin access / cell orientation causing M1-M2 spacing violation
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If DRC markers are at standard-cell pins and report shows M1 spacing < rule and cell is same 2-3 library cells, run pin-access check; if violations are within 1um of pin, it's pin access
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Flip orientation, swap to different VT or size, add placement halo 1-2 tracks around problematic cells

candidate_causes.cause: Minimum area / via enclosure DRC from automatic via doubling
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If DRCs are via enclosure and appear only after double-via or via farm insertion and marker is on via layer, and layer is M1-V1 or M2-V2 in dense area
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Disable double via in hotspot, allow single via with exception, add metal patch to meet min area

candidate_causes.cause: Off-grid / off-track macro pins not on routing grid
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If DRCs cluster around macro pins and macro pins are at x.05 instead of x.0 grid (check 5nm grid vs 1nm manufacturing), and detail router cannot snap
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Snap macro pins to grid in LEF, move macro to routing track, enable off-grid routing in that layer

candidate_causes.cause: Non-default rule or shielding causing spacing to be unresolvable
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If DRCs involve NDR nets and spacing to NDR is > default spacing and NDR nets are in dense area, and default rule vs NDR rule report shows conflict
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Relax NDR spacing in dense channel, reserve shield track, move shielded net to higher layer

candidate_causes.cause: High density + wrong routing layer direction causing odd-cycle
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If DRCs are mostly short with 2-3 net loops and layer assignment shows wrong preferred direction or M3 horizontal used where vertical expected, and congestion map clean but DRCs remain
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Fix preferred direction, add routing layer, add routing blockage to force different layer, re-run with different random seed

ordering_rationale: Check marker location and layer distribution first to separate local pin-access vs global NDR/grid issues because local fixes (cell swap, snap) are cheap and targeted vs wholesale routing changes.
classic_trap: Running more detail-route iterations hoping DRCs clear when markers are stuck at same macro pins - router cannot fix off-grid or pin-access issues no matter how many iterations; placement/floorplan must change.
